portInfo.description: Tilbury puts you on the Thames estuary with Gravesend across the water and London as a deliberate transfer, not a stroll. Follow Ferry Road / cruise-terminal signage; the main port/Asda-style entrance is the wrong gate for cruise passengers. Local Thames-side time is realistic on short calls; Tower of London or museum days need a pre-booked transfer and an honest buffer.

facts.established: Port developed in the late 19th century

size.citySize: Part of Greater London metropolitan area

climate.description: Mild climate with moderate rainfall throughout the year

politics.visaRequirements: Visa requirements vary by nationality. UK not in Schengen Area.
politics.entryRequirements: Valid passport required. Some nationalities need visa in advance.

gettingThere.publicTransport: Train from Tilbury Town to London stations

thingsToDo.intro: Pick one neighbourhood or excursion scale and keep time for the gangway queue on the way back.
topThings: Tilbury / Thames-side orientation (fort area / landing-stage views): allow 60–90 minutes without leaving for London.
Tower of London: allow 2–3 hours inside plus the Tilbury–London transfer pair. Book timed entry.
British Museum: allow 2–3 hours plus transfers.
Organised London coach tour: only with confirmed ship-timed return. Estimate markers: transfers 90–120 min each way.
thingsToDo.shortCall: Stay near the port area and keep a generous buffer before all-aboard.
thingsToDo.standardCall: Combine a central walk, one attraction, and lunch if times allow—start back well before all-aboard.
thingsToDo.longerCall: A second stop or coach outing is realistic only with confirmed transport and an eight-hour or longer window.
thingsToDo.practicalTip: Follow Ferry Road cruise-terminal signs; the Asda/main port entrance is the wrong gate. Photograph the terminal façade before boarding a London coach.
